newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso could eventually adjust, official says.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso could eventually adjust, official says.

text.p: The Mexican peso, extremely stable of late, could eventually adjust and move to a new weaker level, the country's deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Wednesday in a conference call with financial analysts.
He said the crucial issue would be to prevent any volatility in the exchange market from affecting other financial markets.
"The most important thing is that volatility doesn't contaminate other markets," he said.
Werner said that good global liquidity and improving economic conditions in Mexico have helped delay any adjustment in the Mexican currency.
The currency has recently moved in a predictable pattern against the U.S. dollar, with periods of stability alternating with short-lived periods of weakness.
Werner also said that there will not be any minimum wage increase in Mexico for the rest of the year.
"We will not see any minimum wage increase for the rest of the year. There are no surprises on the wage front," he said.
